messages.subject: MSstats without evidence.txt
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm trying to run MSstats on a PRIDE dataset that has been processed with MaxQuant (PXD014156 <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD014156>). This project provides the proteinGroups.txt file, but not evidence.txt. I'm wondering if its possible to run MSstats without the MaxQuant evidence file, for this experiment?
Thanks,
Lincoln

messages.subject: Re: MSstats without evidence.txt
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lincoln,

Unfortunately the MaxQuant converter requires the evidence.txt file. This is because we work on the PSM level and the proteinGroups.txt file does not contain the information we need.

Best,
Devon

messages.subject: NA_NA field after `quantification`
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to use MSstats to impute missing values in the PRIDE dataset PXD014525 <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD014525>. This dataset was processed with MaxQuant and all of the requisite MSstats input files are present on PRIDE. Here is a screenshot of my annotations file (below, left).  As far as I can tell, the run IDs in my annotations file match up with the run IDs in the evidence file. Yet when I perform the `dataProcess` and `quantification` steps, I get a dataframe with only two columns, instead of the expected 40. The column names of this output dataframe are Protein and NA_NA (shown below, right).

I'd like to generate an imputed matrix where rows are proteins and columns are runs. What is going wrong here?
Thanks

messages.subject: 0 vs 1 Tech replicates problem in the dataProcess function
messages.subject_clean: 0 vs 1 Tech replicates problem in the dataProcess function
messages.body_plain:
Hey everyone,

In the output data of the dataProcess function, I get 0 in the Tech. replicates for the 21 control samples, and 1 for the 41 disease samples (see screenshot 1) knowing that both don't have any tech replicates so the correct number should be 1, right?

With another dataset, I got 0 in the tech. replicates for both controls (15) and disease samples (9) knowing that I don't have any tech replicates in the study (see screenshot 2).

The only common trait among samples with 0 tech replicates in the dataProcess output is that they're fractionated samples.

I am wondering if it's normal to get 0 for fractionated samples or if there's something I need to change in order to get 1 (which is the usual normal).

Thank you!

Best,
Ayman Reffai

messages.subject: Arranging processed data in MSstats format
messages.subject_clean: Arranging processed data in MSstats format
messages.body_plain:
Dear MS Stats Help Team,

I would like to perform statistical analysis, suing the Shiny App, on already processed data sets (normalized abundance) from DDA-TMT runs (analyzed using Proteome Discover). This was a shotgun proteomics run for 20 samples (TMT-10 plex/2 runs, 4 experimental groups with 5 replicates per group). I tried to arrange the data in the attached format with the accompanying annotation file but the shiny app would just crashed. Can you please let me know what is the best way to approach this. Thank you.

--Regards
Banrida
messages.body_snippet:
Dear MS Stats Help Team,

I would like to perform statistical analysis, suing the Shiny App, on already processed data sets (normalized abundance) from DDA-TMT runs (analyzed using Proteome Discover).

messages.subject: Re: Arranging processed data in MSstats format
messages.subject_clean: Arranging processed data in MSstats format
messages.body_plain:
Hi Banrida,

It looks like your PD output is not the PSM file. MSstats requires the PSM file in order to work correctly.

For an example of how the data should look, you can run the following code in R:

library(MSstatsTMT)
head(raw.pd)

Best,
Devon
